evidence.source: CUHK 漢語多功能字庫 (Multi-function Chinese Character Database)
evidence.text: The entry displays two seal-script examples and eleven bronze-script examples for 關. Its analysis records competing accounts: bronze graphs are described as 門 plus 卝, with 卝 variously treated as a phonetic, a prototype of 關, or a depiction of two bars and a looped lock; it also records forms with 串, identified there as phonetic. The page cites the 鄂君啟舟節 for a bronze-period use meaning a frontier pass. These are the database’s reported analyses and attestations, not a resolution of the competing graphic readings.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.text: The official site describes its character-evolution database as covering oracle-bone, bronze, Warring States, seal and clerical-transition forms. The entry-specific query URL for 關 could not be accessed through the web tool, so no Xiaoxuetang form or label is selected here.
evidence.title: 小學堂

evidence.text: The official notice says glyph images and glyph-attribute information obtained through the site’s query interface are released under CC0 1.0. This applies to query-interface images and attributes, not to other linked content or other Academia Sinica sites.
evidence.title: 版權聲明

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry lists 关 and 関 among variants of 關. For 関 it quotes older lexicographic sources and classifies it as a variant, but this entry does not establish that simplified 关 descends from 関. It also records a cautious proposal that a form in the bronze inscription called 關中布 resembles, and may be the source of, 𨳹; that is a separate proposed relation.
evidence.title: [A04398] 關 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: CUHK 漢語多功能字庫, quoting 說文解字 and summarizing traditional analyses
evidence.text: The entry reproduces 說文’s analysis of 關 as 从門、𢇅聲 and defines it as wood laid crosswise to secure a doorway. This supports 門 as the stated semantic component and 𢇅 as the stated phonetic component in the seal-script analysis. The entry gives 關’s fanqie 古還切 and Middle Chinese rhyme-class information, but the inspected page does not provide a historical reconstruction for 𢇅 itself; a sound comparison between the two is therefore not established here.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: CUHK 漢語多功能字庫, quoting and discussing early textual examples
evidence.text: The database cites the 鄂君啟舟節 inscription for 關 meaning a frontier pass, and cites 《詩經・關雎》 for 關關 as a bird-call expression. It treats these as different textual uses; the page does not establish that the bird-call expression is the same lexical root as ‘barrier’ or establish a semantic path between the two. Its page gives no absolute date for the cited inscription.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.text: The entry gives 關’s fanqie as 古還切 and Middle Chinese category information (initial 見, level tone, 山攝, 刪 rhyme, division 2, rounded). This is Middle Chinese rhyme-table classification rather than an Old Chinese reconstruction. No independently checked historical pronunciation for 𢇅 was found in the inspected pages; therefore no same-system reconstruction comparison is supplied.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

search_audit.query: 關 古文字 字形 金文 說文 門 𢇅
search_audit.outcome: Inspected CUHK entry, Xiaoxuetang technical report and Shuowen.org page. CUHK page supplies labeled bronze and seal glyph links in its page description, but direct images return empty content in the web tool and the entry-specific Xiaoxuetang query URL was inaccessible.

gaps: The entry-specific Xiaoxuetang query for 關 was inaccessible through the web tool, so no exact Xiaoxuetang image URL or label could be verified. The general CC0 notice was inspected, but it does not license an unverified candidate image.

CUHK’s 關 entry reports eleven bronze-script and two seal-script glyph examples, but its linked direct image pages returned no readable contents. Since no direct image URL and provenance record could be verified from the inspected page output, no glyph image is proposed.

No image was visually inspected. The CUHK and Ministry records support candidate forms and textual descriptions only; they do not establish an image candidate’s pixel content or exact artifact identity.
The bronze analysis has competing explanations for 卝 and other components; the inspected page does not settle whether these forms depict a door lock, encode sound, or represent an earlier graph.
The proposed sound role of 𢇅 is supported here as a 說文 assertion. The inspected sources did not provide an independently checked historical pronunciation for 𢇅 to compare with 關.
The bronze-period pass attestation is cited by the CUHK database, but the page inspected does not date that specific inscription; a precise first-attestation date is unresolved.
The bird-call use 關關 and the barrier/door-bar uses remain lexically and semantically unconnected in the inspected sources. No object-name-based whole-graph loan is established.

limitations.text: No candidate image is proposed because inspected source pages did not expose a verifiable, exact direct glyph image with its form label and provenance. The image search included Commons and Academia Sinica; returned Commons material was unrelated, and the Xiaoxuetang query for 關 was inaccessible. The CUHK entry’s image links were present but returned empty page contents through the web tool.
